$comment: Best-practice seeds for the documentation enrichment layer (component-builder Step 4.5, layers 2-3). Sources: W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (roles + keyboard), Material 3, Shopify Polaris, IBM Carbon. These are SEEDS, NOT GOSPEL — they are generic to the archetype, not specific to Jake UI, and any of them may be wrong for a given component. Enrichment only ever fills a block that adoption left absent or empty, and never overwrites imported content. Edit this file rather than the generated records; re-run `npm run docs:enrich`.

frameworkVocabulary.$comment: Layer 3 — variant-meaning wording specialized to project.uiFramework (shadcn). Keyed by variant axis, then value. Only used to fill a meaning that adoption imported as an empty string.

style.outline: Medium emphasis; a bordered alternative to secondary.
style.ghost: Lowest emphasis, for inline or toolbar actions.

tone.neutral: No semantic weight — a plain label or count.
tone.warning: Needs attention but is not blocking.
tone.default: Standard treatment with no semantic weight.

size.small: Dense contexts — tables, toolbars, compact rows.
size.medium: The default in forms and dialogs.
size.sm: Dense contexts — tables, toolbars, compact rows.
size.md: The default in forms and dialogs.
size.default: The standard size — use unless there is a reason not to.

density.comfortable: Default spacing, easier to scan and tap.
density.detailed: Roomier, for richer content than the default carries.

state.empty: No content — show an empty state, not a blank area.
state.interactive: The whole surface responds to pointer and keyboard.
state.disabled: Not available; not focusable and does not respond to input.
state.active: The currently selected item in its group.
state.expanded: Shown at full width, with labels visible.

mode.range: Selects a start and end pair.
mode.modal: Blocks the page behind it until dismissed.
mode.trapFocus: Keeps keyboard focus inside while open.

type.form: Contains editable fields; needs submit and cancel affordances.
type.media: Leads with an image or media block.
type.initials: Falls back to initials when no image is available.
type.status: Carries a presence or status indicator.
type.avatar: Avatar shape — a circular image, or initials when no image is available.
type.required: Marks a field that must be filled before submit.
type.optional: Marks a field that may be left empty.
type.determinate: Progress is known and reported as a proportion of a total.
type.indeterminate: Progress is unknown — show activity, not a percentage.
type.text: Placeholder for a line or block of text.
type.tableRow: Placeholder shaped like a table row.
type.header: The heading region, above the body.
type.footer: The summary or totals region, below the body.
type.rTL: Right-to-left layout — mirrored for RTL locales.

side.right: Opens to the right of the trigger.
side.left: Opens to the left of the trigger.

align.start: Aligns to the trigger's start edge.
align.end: Aligns to the trigger's end edge.

orientation.horizontal: Lays out along the inline axis.
orientation.vertical: Lays out along the block axis.

width.compact: Narrow — for filters and short forms.
width.wide: Roomier — for tables and dense content.

value.indeterminate: Partially selected — some children selected, some not.

disabled.true: Not available; not focusable and does not respond to input.

collapsed.false: Every item is shown in full.
collapsed.true: Middle items are folded behind an overflow affordance.

selected.true: Selected — the active choice in its group.

pressed.false: Off — the toggle is not engaged.

attached.false: Members keep their own borders and are separated by a gap.
attached.true: Members are joined into one continuous control, sharing inner borders.

arrow.false: No pointer — the surface floats free of its trigger.
arrow.true: Shows a pointer aimed at the trigger.

inset.false: Aligned to the container's leading edge.
inset.true: Indented to line up with items that have a leading icon.

alignment.left: Text aligned to the leading edge — the default for labels and prose.
alignment.right: Text aligned to the trailing edge — use for numbers, so digits line up.

emphasis.strong: Heavier weight, to mark the row's key value.

selection.selected: At least one item is selected.
selection.single: One item at a time may be selected.
selection.multiple: Several items may be selected at once.
selection.first: The first option in the group is selected.
selection.second: The second option in the group is selected.

whenToUse: Trigger an action or event — submit, confirm, open a dialog.
whenNotToUse: Navigating between pages or URLs — use a Link.
dos: Lead the label with a verb.
Keep one primary (highest-emphasis) button per view.
Keep labels short — around three words or fewer.
donts: Do not use a button for navigation.
Do not stack multiple primary buttons.
Do not disable a button without telling the user why.

keyboard: Enter and Space activate.
notes: An icon-only button needs an aria-label.
Disabled buttons are not focusable.

whenToUse: Collect a single line of free-form text.
whenNotToUse: Choosing from a fixed set — use Select or Radio Group.
Long multi-line text — use Textarea.
dos: Always pair with a visible label.
Show format hints as helper text.
Reserve space for error text so validation does not shift the layout.
donts: Do not use placeholder text as the only label.
Do not validate on every keystroke before the first blur.

keyboard: Standard text-editing keys.
notes: Every input has a programmatically associated label.
The error state sets aria-invalid and links its message via aria-describedby.

whenToUse: Collect free-form text long enough to need more than one line.
whenNotToUse: A single short value — use Input.
Rich or formatted content — use a rich-text editor, not a plain textarea.
dos: Always pair with a visible label.
Size the default height to the expected answer, so the field itself sets the expectation.
Reserve space for error text so validation does not shift the layout.
Show a character counter whenever a limit is enforced.
donts: Do not use placeholder text as the only label.
Do not silently truncate at a limit — say the limit before it is hit.
Do not make it so short that the user edits through a keyhole.

keyboard: Standard text-editing keys.
Enter inserts a newline; it must not submit the form.
notes: Every textarea has a programmatically associated label.
The error state sets aria-invalid and links its message via aria-describedby.
A character counter is announced politely, not on every keystroke.

whenToUse: Choose one option from a fixed, known list.
Prefer it over a custom control when the platform's own menu is acceptable — it is accessible for free and behaves correctly on mobile.
whenNotToUse: Free-form input — use Input.
Two or three options that fit on screen — use Radio Group; the choices stay visible.
Multi-select, option search, or rich option content — the native control cannot do these.
dos: Always pair with a visible label.
Order options meaningfully — frequency or alphabetically — not by database order.
Make the default either a real default or an explicit unselected prompt.
donts: Do not use the first option as a de facto label.
Do not restyle the platform option menu — only the closed control is yours to style.
Do not use one for a boolean — that is a Checkbox or a Switch.

keyboard: Arrow keys move through options; Enter or Space opens the menu.
Typing letters jumps to matching options.
Escape closes the menu without changing the value.
notes: It is a native select element, so platform semantics come for free — do not re-implement them.
Programmatically associated label; the error state sets aria-invalid and links its message via aria-describedby.

whenToUse: Wrap a form control with its label, helper text, and error message as one unit.
whenNotToUse: A bare control that is already labelled by its surroundings.
Page layout — it composes one field, not a form.
dos: Own the label-to-control association here, so no control has to do it itself.
Reserve space for the error message so validation does not shift the layout.
Keep helper text and error text in the same position.
donts: Do not let the wrapped control render its own second label.
Do not replace helper text with the error — a user often needs both.

notes: Generates the id and binds label-for, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid onto the control it wraps.
The error message is announced politely; it is not a role="alert" per keystroke.

whenToUse: Checkbox or toggle for an independent on/off value.
Radio for one-of-many within a group.
whenNotToUse: A single either/or action that takes effect immediately with no save — prefer a toggle over a checkbox.
A choice that only applies after a separate Save — prefer radio or checkbox over a toggle.
dos: Label the control itself, not only the group.
Make the label clickable.
donts: Do not use a radio group for multi-select.
Do not use a toggle for choices that only apply after a separate Save.

keyboard: Space toggles.
Radio groups move between options with arrow keys.
notes: State is exposed via aria-checked, never by colour alone.

whenToUse: Group related content and actions about a single subject.
whenNotToUse: Primary page layout scaffolding.
A bare list of text.
dos: Make the primary action obvious.
Keep one main call-to-action per card.
donts: Do not nest cards more than one level.
Do not make the whole card and an inner button separately clickable in conflicting ways.

notes: If the whole card is a link or button it needs an accessible name.
Do not bury interactive controls where keyboard users reach them out of order.

whenToUse: Interrupt for a focused task, or a decision that blocks the flow.
whenNotToUse: Non-critical messages — use an inline alert or a toast.
dos: Trap focus while open.
Return focus to the trigger on close.
Provide an explicit close affordance.
donts: Do not stack dialogs.
Do not put long scrolling forms in a small dialog.

keyboard: Escape closes.
Tab cycles within the dialog only.
notes: aria-modal="true", labelled by its title via aria-labelledby.
Focus is trapped within while open.

whenToUse: A short status, count, or category label.
whenNotToUse: Interactive primary actions — use a Button.
dos: Keep text to a word or two.
Bind colour to a semantic tone token.
donts: Do not rely on colour alone to convey status — include text or an icon.

notes: Status is conveyed with text, not colour only (WCAG 1.4.1).
A removable chip's remove control needs an accessible name, e.g. "Remove <label>".

subpart.$comment: Compound-component children (Table / Cell, Popover / Arrow, …). These are not standalone components; the parent is named in the record's own name. Deliberately generic — anything more specific belongs to layer 4.
whenToUse: Only inside its parent component's composition — this is a part, not a standalone component.
whenNotToUse: On its own, outside the parent that owns its behaviour and accessibility wiring.
As a general-purpose layout or text primitive.
dos: Compose it through the parent rather than reaching for it directly.
donts: Do not re-implement the parent's keyboard or focus behaviour on the part.

whenToUse: Let the reader collapse secondary content so the page stays scannable.
whenNotToUse: Content the reader almost always needs — show it instead of hiding it.
Switching between peer views — use Tabs.
dos: Make the trigger the whole header row, not just the chevron.
Write triggers that say what is inside.
donts: Do not hide validation errors or required form fields behind a collapsed section.
Do not animate so slowly that opening feels unresponsive.

keyboard: Enter and Space toggle the section.
Tab moves between triggers.
notes: The trigger is a button carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls.
The panel stays in the accessibility tree only while open.

whenToUse: Deliver an in-page message about the state of the view or a task.
whenNotToUse: A decision that must block the flow — use a Dialog.
Transient confirmation of a completed action — use a toast.
dos: Say what happened and what to do next.
Place it next to what it refers to.
donts: Do not stack several alerts competing for attention.
Do not signal severity with colour alone — pair it with an icon and text.

notes: Only an urgent, interrupting message should use role="alert"; a static one uses role="status" or no live region at all.
A dismissible alert's close control needs an accessible name.

whenToUse: Represent a person, account, or organisation compactly.
whenNotToUse: Decorative imagery, or a general-purpose image container.
dos: Fall back to initials, then to a generic placeholder, when no image loads.
Keep the shape consistent across the product.
donts: Do not put meaning in the avatar alone — pair it with a name where identity matters.

notes: A decorative avatar beside a visible name is alt=""; a standalone one needs the name as its accessible name.
A status dot needs a text equivalent, not colour alone.

whenToUse: Show where the current page sits in a hierarchy, and offer a way back up.
whenNotToUse: Flat sites with no hierarchy.
Step-by-step progress through a flow — use a stepper.
dos: Render the current page as plain text, not a link.
Collapse the middle rather than wrapping to a second line.
donts: Do not use it to record visit history — it reflects hierarchy, not the back button.

notes: Wrap in a nav with an accessible name such as "Breadcrumb".
Mark the current page with aria-current="page".
Separators are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

whenToUse: Pick a date, or a start and end pair, where the calendar context matters.
whenNotToUse: A date the user knows by heart, such as a birthdate — a plain text field is faster.
Coarse periods like a month or quarter — offer a Select.
dos: Allow typing the date as well as picking it.
State the expected format next to the field.
Disable out-of-range dates rather than rejecting them after submit.
donts: Do not force calendar navigation for dates far from today.
Do not assume a locale's week start or date order.

keyboard: Arrow keys move by day, PageUp and PageDown by month.
Escape closes the calendar and returns focus to the field.
notes: The grid is a table with aria-selected on the chosen day.
Announce the focused date in full, not just the day number.

whenToUse: Reveal a pattern, comparison, or trend that a table would bury.
whenNotToUse: Precise values the reader needs to read off exactly — use a table.
A single number — use a stat or a Badge.
dos: Label axes and units directly.
Order categories meaningfully, not alphabetically by accident.
Bind series colour to semantic tokens so themes carry through.
donts: Do not distinguish series by colour alone — vary shape, pattern, or direct labels.
Do not truncate a bar chart's value axis away from zero.

notes: Give the chart a text alternative that states the takeaway, not just the chart type.
Offer the underlying data as a table for screen-reader and keyboard users.

whenToUse: Give keyboard-first users a fast path to any command or destination.
whenNotToUse: The primary means of discovering features — it supplements navigation, it does not replace it.
A small fixed set of options — use a Select or a menu.
dos: Show recent or suggested items before the user types.
Group results and label the groups.
Show the keyboard shortcut that opens it somewhere discoverable.
donts: Do not hide destructive commands in it without a confirmation step.
Do not leave an empty result set unexplained.

keyboard: Arrow keys move through results, Enter runs the highlighted one.
Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
notes: The input owns focus and points at the list via aria-controls and aria-activedescendant.
Announce the result count as it changes.

whenToUse: Present records across shared columns, for comparison, scanning, or exact reading.
whenNotToUse: Page layout — use a grid.
A handful of key-value pairs — use a description list.
dos: Right-align numbers so digits line up.
Keep the header visible while the body scrolls.
Give empty, loading, and error states real treatments.
donts: Do not hide the only route to an action behind row hover.
Do not let a wide table break the page — let the table itself scroll.

keyboard: Interactive cells are reachable in reading order.
notes: Header cells are th with the right scope; a caption names the table.
Sortable headers carry aria-sort, and the control is a button inside the th.

whenToUse: Offer a list of actions from a trigger, when showing them all would crowd the view.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a form value — use a Select; a menu fires actions, it does not hold state.
Primary navigation — use a navigation menu.
dos: Group related items and separate the groups.
Put destructive items last and mark them.
Show shortcuts alongside the items that have them.
donts: Do not nest submenus more than one level deep.
Do not hide the only route to a critical action inside a menu.

keyboard: Arrow keys move between items, Enter activates.
Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Typing a letter jumps to the next item starting with it.
notes: The trigger carries aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
Focus moves into the menu on open and back to the trigger on close.

whenToUse: Name or clarify a control whose purpose is not obvious from its label alone.
whenNotToUse: Content the user must read to proceed — a tooltip is unreachable on touch and easy to miss.
Anything interactive: links, buttons, or text to copy — use a Popover.
dos: Keep it to a short phrase.
Attach it to the control itself, so it is reachable by keyboard focus.
donts: Do not put a tooltip on a non-focusable element.
Do not repeat the visible label verbatim.
Do not place essential or interactive content inside one.

keyboard: Shows on focus as well as hover.
Escape dismisses it.
notes: Referenced by the control via aria-describedby.
Stays visible long enough to read, and while the pointer is over it.

whenToUse: Show secondary content or a small task in context, anchored to its trigger.
whenNotToUse: A decision that must block the flow — use a Dialog.
A plain text hint — use a Tooltip.
A list of actions — use a menu.
dos: Anchor it to the trigger and flip it when it would overflow the viewport.
Give it an explicit close affordance.
Return focus to the trigger on close.
donts: Do not open one from inside another.
Do not put a long scrolling form in one.

keyboard: Escape closes.
Tab moves through the content, then out.
notes: The trigger carries aria-expanded and aria-controls.
A popover holding a form should trap focus; a non-modal one should not.

whenToUse: Preview the thing behind a link on hover, without making the reader navigate.
whenNotToUse: Content the user needs — hover is unavailable on touch and to many keyboard users.
Anything required to complete a task.
dos: Open and close on a delay, so passing the pointer over does not trigger it.
Keep it open while the pointer travels into it.
Treat everything in it as an enhancement of the link's own destination.
donts: Do not place the only copy of an action inside one.
Do not open it on click — that is a Popover.

notes: Reachable on keyboard focus, or its content must exist elsewhere.
Escape dismisses it.

whenToUse: Reinforce a label, or stand in for one where the metaphor is unambiguous and repeated.
whenNotToUse: Carrying meaning that has no text anywhere near it.
Illustration — use an image.
dos: Take icons from the mapped set rather than pasting one-off SVG.
Size and colour them from tokens so they track the text they sit beside.
Keep one metaphor for one meaning across the product.
donts: Do not use an icon alone for a destructive or unusual action.
Do not rotate or recolour an icon to mean something new.

notes: A decorative icon beside text is aria-hidden="true".
A meaningful standalone icon needs a text alternative on it or on its control.

whenToUse: Name a form control, so it is identifiable before and after it is filled.
whenNotToUse: Helper text, format hints, or validation messages — those are separate elements.
A section heading — use a heading.
dos: Keep the label visible; do not swap it for a placeholder.
Mark required fields consistently, and say what the marker means once.
Write it as a noun phrase, in sentence case.
donts: Do not mark both required and optional fields — pick whichever is rarer.
Do not truncate a label; shorten the wording instead.

notes: Bound to its control by for/id, so clicking the label focuses the control.
Its text is the control's accessible name — keep it stable.

whenToUse: Present the product's top-level destinations, with room for grouped sub-items.
whenNotToUse: Firing actions — use a menu.
A single flat list of two or three links — plain links are enough.
dos: Mark the current destination.
Keep the order stable between sessions and roles.
donts: Do not hide a whole section behind hover alone.
Do not nest destinations deeper than two levels.

keyboard: Arrow keys move within a group; Tab moves between groups.
notes: Wrapped in a nav with an accessible name.
The current destination carries aria-current="page".

whenToUse: Keep navigation persistently in view alongside the main content.
whenNotToUse: Fewer than about five destinations — a horizontal bar reads faster.
Page content or filters that belong in the main column.
dos: Remember the expanded or collapsed choice across sessions.
Keep icons meaningful when collapsed, and add tooltips for their labels.
Move to an overlay drawer at narrow widths.
donts: Do not collapse to icons alone where the metaphors are ambiguous.
Do not let the sidebar scroll the whole page.

keyboard: The collapse control is focusable and labelled.
notes: The collapse toggle carries aria-expanded.
When collapsed, each item still needs an accessible name.

whenToUse: A single destination within sidebar navigation.
whenNotToUse: Firing an action rather than navigating — use a Button.
dos: Make the whole row the hit target, not just the text.
Show the active state from the route, not from click state.
donts: Do not signal the active item by colour alone.

notes: It is a link; the active one carries aria-current="page".
Its icon is decorative when the label is visible.

whenToUse: Break a long result set into pages the reader can move through and return to.
whenNotToUse: A feed meant to be browsed continuously — use infinite scroll or a load-more control.
Result sets short enough to show at once.
dos: Show the current page and the total.
Keep previous and next in the same place as the page count changes.
Disable rather than hide the controls at the first and last page.
donts: Do not reset filters or sort when the page changes.
Do not make the hit targets smaller than the surrounding controls.

keyboard: Every control is reachable in reading order.
notes: Wrapped in a nav named e.g. "Pagination".
The current page carries aria-current="page"; disabled controls stay announced.

whenToUse: Show that work is underway, and how far along it is when that is known.
whenNotToUse: Waits short enough that the indicator flashes — show nothing.
Content-shaped placeholders while a view loads — use Skeleton.
dos: Use the determinate form whenever a total is known.
Say what is happening in text beside the bar.
Keep it in place until the work actually finishes.
donts: Do not fake determinate progress.
Do not let a bar sit at 100% without resolving.

notes: Determinate sets aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax.
Indeterminate omits aria-valuenow.
Named by aria-labelledby, or aria-label when no visible label exists.

whenToUse: Confine overflow to one region so the page itself does not scroll.
whenNotToUse: The main page scroll — leave that to the browser.
Hiding content the reader is unlikely to look for.
dos: Leave a visible cue that there is more to see.
Keep native keyboard and wheel scrolling working.
donts: Do not nest scroll areas along the same axis.
Do not hide the scrollbar so thoroughly that the overflow is invisible.

keyboard: The region is focusable so it can be scrolled by keyboard.
notes: A scrollable region needs a tabindex and an accessible name.
Do not suppress the native scrollbar on platforms that always show one.

whenToUse: Switch between peer views of the same subject, within one context.
whenNotToUse: Steps in a sequence — use a stepper.
Content the reader needs to compare side by side, or to find with the browser's search.
Navigating to a different page — use links.
dos: Keep one tab selected at all times.
Keep labels short enough to fit on one line without wrapping.
Preserve each panel's state when switching away and back.
donts: Do not scroll or wrap tabs into a second row — reconsider the grouping.
Do not hide required form fields in an unselected tab.

keyboard: Arrow keys move between tabs; Home and End jump to the first and last.
Tab moves from the tab list into the active panel.
notes: Each tab carries aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel is labelled by its tab.
Only the selected tab is in the tab order.

whenToUse: Mark a boundary between groups that spacing alone does not make clear.
whenNotToUse: Where whitespace already separates the groups.
Decoration, or as a border around a region.
dos: Bind it to a border token so it tracks the theme.
donts: Do not use a run of separators to create rhythm.

notes: Purely visual separators are aria-hidden="true".
One that genuinely divides groups keeps role="separator" and its orientation.

whenToUse: Hold the shape of content that is loading, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.
whenNotToUse: Waits short enough that it flashes.
Work with a known duration or total — use Progress.
An error or an empty result — those need their own states.
dos: Match the real content's dimensions closely.
Show a small representative number of placeholders, not a full page of them.
donts: Do not leave skeletons up indefinitely when a request fails.
Do not animate so strongly that the page appears to be moving.

notes: Hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true"; announce loading once, in a live region.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion by dropping the shimmer.

whenToUse: Pick from a continuous or coarsely stepped range where the relative position matters more than the exact figure.
whenNotToUse: A precise value the user knows — use a number input.
Ranges so wide that a pixel is worth many units.
Fewer than about five discrete options — use radios or a segmented control.
dos: Show the current value as text next to the track.
Make the thumb large enough to hit on touch.
Pair it with a number input when precision matters.
donts: Do not use one for a value with a required exact entry.
Do not hide the minimum and maximum.

keyboard: Arrow keys move by one step; PageUp and PageDown by a larger one.
Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum.
notes: Carries aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuetext where a raw number would not read well.
The thumb is the focusable element and carries the accessible name.

mapping.$comment: Jake UI component name -> archetype. Anything unlisted takes the documented fallback: no dos/donts are invented, and only the accessibility block is seeded where the W3C APG pattern is unambiguous. `null` means deliberately unmapped.
mapping.$inputFamilyComment: Textarea, Native Select and Field were all mapped to 'input' until 9 Aug 2026. The seed text was self-contradictory on all three — it told Textarea 'collect a single line' and 'for long multi-line text use Textarea', and told Native Select not to be used for 'choosing from a fixed set'. Each now has its own archetype. Do not re-collapse them.
mapping.Label: label
mapping.$subpartComment: Compound-component children. A `/ Root Composition` is NOT listed here — it is the assembled component, so it takes the parent's archetype above.
